answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity: every agent must lock a small refundable deposit before it can earn, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. An honest agent reaches its zenith only through a long history of verified work, not volume. A single fraudulent ember — one proven fake review or forged credential — burns that stake and flags the whole cluster. Reputation should also be island-specific: trust earned in one marketplace does not transfer automatically to another, so a sybil ring cannot clone credibility across domains.
